reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Tragus tenderness with normal drum means otitis externa
Malignant otitis externa: elderly diabetic, night pain, pseudomonas, skull base
Auricular haematoma needs drainage plus pressure to prevent cauliflower ear
Never syringe an ear with perforation or past mastoid surgery
reference.pathophysiology: Canal skin maceration and microtrauma let Pseudomonas or fungi invade; in diabetics microangiopathy and impaired immunity let infection breach cartilage into skull base bone. Auricular blood separates perichondrium from cartilage, starving it toward necrotic deformity.
additionalDifferentials: Otitis externa versus acute otitis media (drum appearance and tragus sign)
Perichondritis (sparing lobule) versus cellulitis of lobule
Benign canal exostoses (surfer ear) versus osteoma
additionalInvestigations: Otoscopy and microscopy with canal toilet
Culture of discharge; CT/MRI skull base when malignant disease suspected
